acv.quote: It would have been about seventy-five K a year.

data.reason: The CFO froze all new vendor projects after a Q3 miss. No cost case in Pikeview's own numbers ever reached her. Renee calls it timing, but that gap went unfixed for a month.

trigger.action: Aim messaging at teams whose pricing changes take a full quarter.
trigger.why: Nothing big started this. Owen had long-standing pain with a homegrown system and no deadline.
trigger.quote: every pricing change takes them a quarter

decider.action: Get the CFO into the deal before the contract goes out.
decider.why: Renee never spoke to Diane. Owen planned to bring her in only at the end.

competitor.action: Treat doing nothing as the rival and show what it costs.
competitor.why: Renee believes Owen looked at no other vendor, and finance saw the project as 'a nice to have'.
competitor.quote: It was us against doing nothing.

message.action: Replace the revenue-growth claim with the fast price-change story.
message.why: Owen rejected the revenue pitch, but the price-change demo won him over.
message.quote: we're not trying to grow revenue with billing

proof.action: Build a cost worksheet that uses the buyer's own numbers.
proof.why: Owen asked for payback and Renee sent the general ROI deck, which he couldn't take to Diane.
proof.quote: I can't get this past Diane without a number that's ours.

words.action: Call slow homegrown billing 'a tax on the roadmap' in our copy.
words.why: Owen described his own problem this way, in his own words.
